item.text: {"text":"The closest recent match is [Ti-CoRe (2026)](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/cpe.70585), which introduces a T-BERT encoder incorporating time-interval awareness into BERT4Rec, alongside contrastive learning. The foundational [TiSASRec paper](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) models pairwise interaction intervals together with absolute positions: useful temporal machinery to adapt inside BERT4Rec without adopting its causal backbone. [TiM4Rec (2025)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925231225019423) explores user-adaptive temporal scaling and localized temporal priors. Its backbone is outside the permitted family, but its distinction between global activity pace and local timing provides relevant design inspiration. These papers support investigating temporal relevance; they do not establish gains on the pinned four-category benchmark.\n\nA suitable experimental hypothesis is one BERT4Rec network with learned, bucketed log-time interval biases in bidirectional attention, retaining content attention and positional embeddings. Unconstrained interval biases can preserve older relevant interactions rather than imposing universal exponential decay; content attention can distinguish coherent repeated interests from isolated events. This is a proposed adaptation, not a demonstrated result from these sources. Compare it directly against the existing terminal-prefix objective with identical training and validation settings. Preserve [BERT4Rec’s masked-target formulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) and appended-mask inference. Use only observed history timestamps; assign the prediction mask a consistent history-derived time reference rather than the withheld target timestamp. Keep temporal parameters jointly trained within the single category model, and judge improvement by macro validation HR@10."}
